title: perf: extract proven single-image paths without rebuilding glossary JSON
body:
## Problem

After native term-bank validation, media extraction decodes and parses each media-hinted glossary again. On the pinned VNDB corpus this reconstructs 84,398,732 bytes of JSON across 146,725 projected rows.

## Change

Add an allocation-free native semantic projection that returns a quoted path span only when the complete glossary yields exactly one image path. The worker decodes that token directly. Missing, empty, multiple-image, unsupported or unproven cases retain the existing JavaScript collector.

The projection follows the collector's nested-content edges, image-selector precedence, escaped keys and duplicate-last-key semantics. It reads only the worker's current bounded source span and introduces no per-row columns, heap arena, dictionary threshold, schema change or altered persisted content.

The source-bound WASM artifact was regenerated with pinned LLVM 21.1.8. Its size increases by 4,546 bytes; package and memory effects remain qualification gates.

## Validation

- 222 focused tests, including real compressed-worker transport, duplicate and escaped fields, malformed ignored fields, 256-level nesting, source bounds, fallback guards and stable results after heap reuse.
- Main/test TypeScript and changed-file ESLint pass.
- Complete 170-group VNDB differential: all 6,648,310 rows, every output column, content slab, key plan, prepared index and media row remain deeply equal.
- With the browser's effective production flags, all 146,725 projected rows use the native path. All 146,570 unique image paths remain.
- Full-glossary JSON.parse calls fall from 146,725 to zero; their 84,398,732 input bytes are eliminated. UTF-8 decoder input falls to 2,391,178 bytes of path tokens.
- An independently retained replay with native escaped-key admission disabled exercised 429 conservative source-range fallbacks and produced identical outputs as well. It is fallback coverage, not the effective production route.
- The release archive grows by 2,785 bytes (baseline 17,265,196 bytes), including the shipped C source and pinned WASM.

## Qualification

Frozen on develop `bbccabd520972cc351a65d9f545bd5369b6e9747`. Fixed complete-import browser cohorts, independent media readback and separate process-tree memory checks are being acquired. The byte-work reduction above is correctness/component evidence, not a full-import speedup claim. This remains a draft until qualification finishes.

Original implementation; no third-party implementation code was copied.
